Service survived to a later call (PPID 1, reparented — good, detached). curl returned 200 with body exactly "p6-service-ok" (13 bytes, no trailing newline).

Now let's also verify content exactly matches with a byte comparison, then stop the service and verify it's stopped.

Also check service.log for the request access log line as extra evidence. Then stop: kill 902, verify port free, curl should fail.

Let me do verification + stop.

Careful: I want to keep evidence of the running state. Do the exact-match check before stopping.

{"command": "cd /home/rimuru/Projects/Code/for_fun/TeamAgents/review/eval/r2-p6/runs/2026-09-27-pilot-bc/work/service-check.B.1
echo "--- exact body check (printf p6-service-ok | cmp -) ---"
printf 'p6-service-ok' | cmp - service.txt && echo "EXACT_MATCH: service.txt == b'p6-service-ok' (no trailing newline)"
echo "--- byte count ---"; wc -c < service.txt
echo "--- access log from service.log ---"; cat service.log

echo "=== STOPPING SERVICE ==="
kill 902
for i in $(seq 1 20); do kill -0 902 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.2; done
if kill -0 902 2>/dev/null; then echo "still alive, sending SIGKILL"; kill -9 902; sleep 0.5; fi
echo "--- ps after stop ---"; ps -o pid,stat,cmd -p 902 2>&1 | tail -n +1
echo "--- pgrep after stop ---"; pgrep -af "service.py" || echo "no service.py process found"
echo "--- curl after stop (expect failure) ---"
curl -sS -m 5 http://127.0.0.1:8765/health; echo "curl_exit=$?""}
